Hi Elena — thanks for sending this over and outlining the priorities. We've started filling the workbook; attached is a preliminary PDF response with our top-level positions and points-of-contact. A few clarifying notes up front:

- We separate retention tiers by event class (authentication, control-plane changes, inference inputs/outputs, system telemetry). Typical default retention: 90 days (hot), 1 year (cold), archival beyond 7 years via reserved contracts. Customers can customize per-model and per-route.
- Export formats: NDJSON (preferred for event streams), Parquet (columnar for analytics), CSV (small-scope exports). We also support transparent token-level metadata in exports when enabled (this creates larger payloads and is opt-in).
- For forensic exports we provide a manifest with SHA-256 hashes per file, a signing timestamp, and optional notarization via our HSM integration.
- SLA for on-demand bulk extracts depends on size and retention tier; rough guidance in the attached PDF.

Ben (cc) will add technical export mechanics (presigned S3 delivery, streaming extracts, and chain-of-custody templates). Marissa will coordinate delivery timelines and legal artifacts.

If you'd like, we can provide a short sample NDJSON manifest (sanitized) and a chain-of-custody template — Ben can drop those in the next message.

Best,

Elena — following up with the technical specifics Hannah mentioned. Inline answers to the workbook items you flagged: 

1) Retention tiers and lifecycle enforcement
- Event classes: auth_events, api_requests, inference_records, config_changes, system_telemetry.
- Hot storage (0-90 days): SSD-backed, low-latency access for investigation.
- Warm storage (90-365 days): optimized for cost with fast bulk-read.
- Cold/archival (365+ days): compressed object storage; retrievals are batched.
- TTL policies are customer-configurable at route/model granularity; we support preservation locks for legal holds (immutable until released by customer).

2) Export mechanics and formats
- Supported deliverables: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Parquet, CSV. For large-scale exports we stream NDJSON into compressed chunked objects (.ndjson.gz) and provide a signed manifest.
- Token provenance: we can include token-level metadata (prompt id, model version, token-reconstruction traces). This is opt-in due to size and privacy impacts; when enabled it's placed in separate artifact files (index + payload) so customers can choose what to ingest.

3) Integrity & chain-of-custody
- Each exported chunk includes SHA-256 and size metadata in the manifest. Manifests are HSM-signed (RSASSA-PSS) and include a UTC timestamp (ISO8601).
- We optionally notarize manifests via a third-party timestamping authority on request for high-assurance workflows.
- Sample manifest fields (export_manifest_sample.ndjson attached): file_name, sha256, bytes, event_count, start_time, end_time, retention_tier, region, signed_by.

4) SLA & delivery timelines
- On-demand extracts: small (<=100GB) typical delivery 24-72 hours; medium (100GB-1TB) 3-7 days; large (>1TB) quoted per-request with parallelization. These windows assume preserved snapshots and no legal/IT blocks.

5) Redaction & PII handling
- We offer configurable redaction pipelines: 
  - Pattern-based redaction (regex allowlist/denylist) applied during export.
  - Field-level redactors for structured payloads (e.g., remove user.email or payment.card_pan).
  - Irreversible redaction: default mode for compliance exports removes content and logs the redaction event (redaction is recorded in the manifest with rationale).
  - Reversible pseudonymization: available under customer-managed KMS keys for scenarios that need reversibility (access controlled by key policies and audit logs).

6) Cross-region and data-sovereignty
- For US accounts we default to US region exports; for EU/EEA accounts we can produce exports that contain only EU-resident artifacts and run the export entirely from EU-backed storage. Cross-region exports are supported but must be declared in the request and may incur additional review.

7) Delivery methods
- S3 presigned object delivery (preferred), secure FTP (legacy), or direct courier of encrypted tapes for extremely large archives (rare). We provide an export manifest and an optional chain_of_custody_template.docx to include signatures at hand-off.

Attachments: export_manifest_sample.ndjson (sanitized), chain_of_custody_template.docx

If you want, we can run a scheduled sample export for a limited dataset so FinTheo can validate the manifests and hashes end-to-end.

Regards,
